chunks: And he was asked about a man who does not know whether he performed three circuits or four. He said:

"Was it a voluntary tawaf or an obligatory one?" He said: "Answer me regarding both of them together." He said: "If it is a voluntary tawaf, then build upon whatever you wish. And if it is an obligatory tawaf, then repeat the tawaf. So if you circled the House in the obligatory tawaf and did not know whether you performed six or seven, then repeat your tawaf. But if you left and that passed you by, then there is nothing upon you."

key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Ka'bah, around which tawaf is performed
key_terms.سَبْعَةً: seven circuits, the complete number for tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافُ نَافِلَةٍ: a voluntary tawaf that is not obligatory
key_terms.فَأَعِدِ الطَّوَافَ: repeat the tawaf from the beginning
key_terms.فَابْنِ عَلَى مَا شِئْتَ: proceed on whichever count you choose in this context of voluntary tawaf

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts the number of circuits during obligatory or voluntary tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on uncertainty during tawaf. In a voluntary tawaf, doubt about the number of circuits is treated with leniency, but in an obligatory tawaf such doubt requires repetition; however, if the person has already left and the opportunity has passed, nothing further is required.
